origins.section: Dropping Integrality Gives an LP Whose Value Bounds Every Plan From Above
A General Integer Branches on Floor and Ceiling
Branching Stops at a Node Whose LP Is Infeasible or Integral

gates.says: all 3 of this quiz's answerable readings held and each was taken over the question as it stands

recorded.prompt:q-bound: Read the whole lesson page, then this question. Using only what the page states, which option does the page decide is correct? Quote or cite the deciding passage.
recorded.outcome:q-bound: z_LP >= z_MILP. That inequality is the "bound" in branch-and-bound. An LP value is an **upper bound**: a number no plan can beat.
recorded.prompt:q-children: Read the whole lesson page, then this question. Using only what the page states, which option does the page decide is correct? Quote or cite the deciding passage.
recorded.outcome:q-children: down: x \le \lfloor v \rfloor, up: x \ge \lceil v \rceil ... Each child keeps the other end of the range it had: the down child keeps its lower bound, the up child its upper bound.
recorded.prompt:q-integral-node: Read the whole lesson page, then this question. Using only what the page states, which option does the page decide is correct? Quote or cite the deciding passage.
recorded.outcome:q-integral-node: An **integral** node, one whose LP solution has no fractional variable, holds a real plan, and that plan is the best one in the node: no plan in the node beats the node's LP, and this plan reaches it. Either way the node is a **leaf**.

recorded.prompt:q-bound:a: Using only what the lesson page states, does a passage of the page rule this option out? Cite the passage, or say none does or that the option is partly true. Be strict.
recorded.outcome:q-bound:a: An LP value is an **upper bound**: a number no plan can beat.
recorded.prompt:q-bound:b: Using only what the lesson page states, does a passage of the page rule this option out? Cite the passage, or say none does or that the option is partly true. Be strict.
recorded.outcome:q-bound:b: The LP's value ... is higher than the best real plan's ... It always is at least as high
recorded.prompt:q-bound:d: Using only what the lesson page states, does a passage of the page rule this option out? Cite the passage, or say none does or that the option is partly true. Be strict.
recorded.outcome:q-bound:d: z_LP >= z_MILP holds for every allowed plan, and the tolerance is only epsilon = 10^-6. No tolerance turns 812.4 into 830, and a plan above the LP value contradicts the bound.
recorded.prompt:q-children:b: Using only what the lesson page states, does a passage of the page rule this option out? Cite the passage, or say none does or that the option is partly true. Be strict.
recorded.outcome:q-children:b: with a general integer, one split narrows the range without fixing the variable.
recorded.prompt:q-children:c: Using only what the lesson page states, does a passage of the page rule this option out? Cite the passage, or say none does or that the option is partly true. Be strict.
recorded.outcome:q-children:c: The children use \lfloor v \rfloor and \lceil v \rceil, whole numbers: "No whole number lies strictly between them". They do not use 3.4 itself.
recorded.prompt:q-children:d: Using only what the lesson page states, does a passage of the page rule this option out? Cite the passage, or say none does or that the option is partly true. Be strict.
recorded.outcome:q-children:d: "For a 0-1 variable, floor is 0 and ceiling is 1". For v = 3.4 the floor is 3 and the ceiling is 4.
recorded.prompt:q-integral-node:a: Using only what the lesson page states, does a passage of the page rule this option out? Cite the passage, or say none does or that the option is partly true. Be strict.
recorded.outcome:q-integral-node:a: Either way the node is a **leaf**. Every other node is split on a fractional variable.
recorded.prompt:q-integral-node:b: Using only what the lesson page states, does a passage of the page rule this option out? Cite the passage, or say none does or that the option is partly true. Be strict.
recorded.outcome:q-integral-node:b: "a child's LP value is never above its parent's ... Going down the tree, bounds only fall". A lower value than the parent is normal and is no reason to drop the node. The integral node's plan is kept ("integral: new incumbent").
recorded.prompt:q-integral-node:c: Using only what the lesson page states, does a passage of the page rule this option out? Cite the passage, or say none does or that the option is partly true. Be strict.
recorded.outcome:q-integral-node:c: "this plan reaches it" and the node is a leaf. The code just records the plan ("search.value, search.plan = lp.value, ..."), with no re-solve of the parent.
